title: Onboarding Guidance: Opening and Activating a Personal Sender Account
content:
A Personal Sender Account application is accepted only when the applicant is at least 18 years old on the application date, counted from the date of birth on the customer profile, and the state of residence on the customer profile is a US state or the District of Columbia.

## Opening level

A new Personal Sender Account opens in status pending verification at one of two opening levels: **Paloma Starter**, or **Paloma Verified** when a government ID and a selfie were captured at sign-up. No other level can be opened directly.

## Activation

The account activates when the identity checks of its opening level pass, and the date the level took effect is the activation date. Activation sets the next periodic review due date to the activation date plus the level's periodic review interval in calendar months — on the same day of the month, falling back to the last day of a shorter month — or leaves it empty when that interval is 0.

| Opening level | Next periodic review due date set at activation |
|---|---|
| Paloma Starter | left empty (the level's periodic review interval is 0) |
| Paloma Verified | the activation date plus the level's periodic review interval in calendar months |

Hypothetical example: an account opened at Paloma Verified that activates on 31 March of a given year, with the 36-month interval the level carries, has its next periodic review due on 31 March three years later; an account activating on 29 February with a 36-month interval falls due on 28 February three years later, the last day of that shorter month.

## Closing an application that never activated

Paloma closes an application only after 30 calendar days have passed since the application was submitted without activation. Days are counted as calendar days from the date the application was submitted (the opened date), so the application can be closed from the opened date plus 30 days onward. A closed application is recorded as closed because verification failed, and the customer may apply again.

| Day counted from the opened date (application not activated) | May Paloma close the application? |
|---|---|
| Day 29 | no |
| Day 30 (the opened date plus 30 days) | yes |
| Any later day | yes |

## Points of judgement

- **Age is read on the application date** from the date of birth in the customer's records; an applicant who turns 18 the day after applying does not meet it on that application.
- **Residence** is read from the customer profile's state of residence; any US state or the District of Columbia meets it.
- **The opening level depends on what was captured at sign-up**, not on what the customer asks for: without both a government ID and a selfie captured at sign-up, the opening level is Paloma Starter.
